summary: the ledger commit that ships a group's last descendant removes the group's file too, and a group with a descendant still queued stays
acceptance: the ledger rewrite retires every group left with no descendant by the set it shipped, in that same commit, and leaves one whose descendants are not all gone
tests: the ledger commit that ships a group's last descendant removes the group's file
a group with a descendant still queued stays in the queue
a group whose last descendant is itself a group leaves in the same commit
a group left empty by a partial ship of its descendants stays in the queue
notes: The rewrite already takes a shipped-tag set and already `git rm`s exactly those files; the group's removal is a second pass over the same set, never a second commit. The walk is the one the footprint union needs.
